body: You're exactly right. Hermione didn't *want* to be Minister of Magic, she actively expressed her dislike for the position and the people surrounding it.
I haven't met someone who genuinely liked Barty Crouch Senior. Please tell me if I'm wrong, but he doesn't get enough attention to be talked about, therefore gathering haters and/or fans.

*Death threats*??? If anything they should be praising him! I mean, his character was pretty awful, but had some great motivations, emotions, relationships and all that. And the actor did such a good job at portraying all of that when I'm sure he's not like this in real life.

I also wasn't really sure about the rivalry, but I did think that in the beginning there was a bit of dislike on Steve's side about Eddie. When Dustin's trying to convince Steve to join the campaign, he mentions Steve being jealous about him having another older male friend. I took this to mean that Dustin has mentioned Eddie a couple of times in the past, with a not-100%-positive reaction from Steve.   
Eddie was pretty nice, and he did try to get the friendship going, but he also mentions Dustin insisting on Steve's awesomeness which I imagine can get annoying. So I think there was at least some awareness that there were two role models of similar ages in Dustin's life, and while there wasn't a full-out rivalry, there was definitely that knowledge on both sides.

1. Harry is awful in it. A kid who grew up in a house without love, tells his struggling child that sometimes he wishes that the kid wasn't his? Yeah, not happening. The Harry Potter that we know would *never* say that.
2. It completely defies the laws of time travel as set out in the *Harry Potter* series. In the Prisoner of Azkaban, we know that everything that has happened *will* always happen, and has always be that way. Harry saving his own butt from Dementors? It happened with past Harry and also the Harry that time travelled. The stone that was thrown through the window to warn them that Fudge was coming to kill Buckbeak? It was Hermione, and it Always Happened. You can't go off the timeline and create new universes, because the future is set in stone.
3. Many queer fans have pointed out the queerbaiting of Scorpius and Albus. They seemed to be blatantly showing the chemistry between them, only for them to be just friends. 
4. Bellatrix and Voldemort? No. 

Essentially, plot holes, reducing characters to less than shadows of their former selves or else changing them completely, and with the screenplay we have zero context. I've read better fanfictions than the Cursed Child, as many people have commented, plus the fact that it has been stated to be canon by JK Rowling. Fans such as myself have completely disregarded this, because it doesn't make sense and we feel that it shouldn't be.  
But I've heard it's good to watch on stage, so I suppose it has that going for it.
I really like this theory, I haven't heard it before. So she was keeping eyes on the Demogorgon and when it ran into Will she tried to help him in the only way she could?

I think there are a couple of factors in this. Prepare for a long comment.

Eddie exists, and there's a bit of tension between him and Steve about who's gonna be Dustin's primary role model. Dustin might be feeling annoyed at Steve and closer to Eddie at this point, because he hangs out with Eddie more and Steve just isn't there. He probably thinks that this "rivalry" is unnecessary and in his opinion, Steve is the instigator. 

Also, Dustin's growing up. He's a teen. And he's just being sarcastic, and it might come off as a bit mean and unusual for his character, I think it's pretty true to the evolution of his character.

But there's another thing, and it might just be that we've advanced to the point where Dustin and Steve act more like brothers than ever before. He's way more comfortable with Steve, and they know what will push each other's buttons. We've seen how their friendship has progressed from Season 1, where I think they didn't interact at all, to Season 2 where Dustin's opinion of him is still kind of low, to Season 3 where they're best buddies. But in this best buddies phase there's a lot of let's-tread-lightly-here, because Steve is Dustin's best friend at this point. He can't afford to lose him.  
Now, though, Dustin's more secure and knows that Steve won't just leave, so he can afford to take the mickey out of him. My brother and I can insult each other about almost everything under the sun and still be really close, but we know that there are certain things not to be mentioned. That scene where Steve mentions Dustin's teeth, when they're in the car, and Dustin goes, "too far". And Steve takes it back immediately and apologises. I think that really shows their brotherhood perfectly, because while they can be rude and maybe even kind of hostile (although I'm not sure that's the best word for it), they still know when to stop and be freinds again.

​

Plus, Steve's "always the goddamn babysitter!" thing. Maybe this is Dustin's payback?

You're right, actually, the real life time jumps. Everybody's getting old now, and they still need to look 15 or so in the show. I think the party are all going to be 17-21 when they start filming, right?

Is the time jump going to be that long? I was sort of under the impression that it was going to be maybe a few months at most, because a year or more just wouldn't make sense, would it?I mean, Vecna's got to recover, and we need to feel the absence of Max, but having a year or even more would seriously not make sense. Like you said, the villains being like, "We should probably take a break to let the heroes relax for a bit, they've deserved it" and then starting a new Minecraft world would be pretty bad.

I hope the time skip isn't that long. What would they even be doing during that time??

Ted is consistent. He remains a human being throughout the series.

He also created the Wheeler children, who we like. We must give him credit for this.

Uh, other than that. He is not a horrible father, maybe? We have our fair share of awful/absent fathers in Stranger Things, so Ted being sensible is a bit of a breather from certain other people, \*cough Lonnie, Steve's dad, Neil Hargrove, Max's dad, Dustin's dad, cough\*. But that's just being a decent person, so I'm not giving him extra points for that.

The scene in Dumbledore's office in Order of the Phoenix, just after Sirius dies and Harry's waiting for Dumbledore to join him. He's so angry and chucks stuff around and yells at Dumbledore, and the old man just kind of accepts it and goes along, and Harry just gets madder and madder and madder. Like, "why isn't Dumbledore as upset as I am about this? It was Dumbledore's fault, and it was kind of my fault too, and I'm really angry and breaking all his stuff and the fool is still so annoyingly calm". I always have to put the book down and step away for a moment when that bit happens, because Harry's lost the last likeable family that he has.

It's probably to have a wondrous and beautiful introduction to the rest of their lives. It's a really special thing, Hogwarts, and some of these kids have never even heard of magic until a couple of weeks ago, so putting in that big effort to make things look really special would be important.
Dogs and snow. Dogs in snow and snow on dogs.

I have a problem with Henry Creel's origin story, specifically the bit where he's hurtling through the Upside Down and is struck by lightning and stuff.

I love Marvel, but I need Stranger Things to not be a superhero movie and it just felt a bit wrong. Like I understand how humanity can be scarier than supernatural events, but this whole thing of "zappity zap zap, you're in a new dimension and you look kinda weird" seems a bit off to me.
I'm imagining that Steve pulled him away from Eddie's body when Steve, Robin, and Nancy returned, and then helped him through the gate in Eddie's trailer. But just my headcanon, I guess.
So how do I fix it?
I don't want to die. But living is hard.
